The ship edged toward the glacier at barely a knot, engines murmuring, and the wall of ice grew until it filled the whole windscreen. It was bluer than anyone had expected. Where the sun hit it, the face glowed like glass, and where it fell in shadow it turned the deep color of the sea at night. Chunks the size of cars drifted past the hull, knocking against the steel with a hollow sound. On the bridge, the captain kept one eye on the sonar; the water ahead was shallow in places and the charts were old. Out on deck, a graduate student lifted a camera and found that her hands were shaking, not from the cold but from the plain, overwhelming size of the thing. Somewhere inside it, a crack boomed like thunder.
